Title 3— Executive Order 12393 of November 16, 1982
The Presid en t Establishing an  E m erg en cy  B o ard  T o In vestigate a  D ispute  
B etw een  T he Long Island R ail R o ad  an d  C ertain  L ab or O rga­
nizations
A dispute exists between The Long Island Rail Road and certain labor  
organizations, designated on the list attached hereto and made a part hereof,  
representing employees of The Long Island Rail Road.
The dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended (“the Act”).
The New York Metropolitan Transportation Authority, the parent body of The  
Long Island Rail Road, has requested that the President establish an emergen­
cy board pursuant to Section 9A of the Act.
Section 9A(c) of the Act provides that the President, upon request of a party,  
shall appoint an emergency board to investigate and report on the dispute.
NOW, THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 9A of the Act,  
as amended (45 U.S.C. § 159a), it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Establishm ent o f Board.  There is established, effective November 16,  
1982, a board of three members to be appointed by the President to investigate  
this dispute. No member shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any  
organization of railroad employees or any carrier. The board shall perform its  
functions subject to the availability of funds.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its findings to the President with respect  
to the dispute within 30 days after the date of its creation.
1-103. M aintaining Conditions.  As provided by Section 9A(c) of the Act, as  
amended, from the date of the creation of the Emergency Board, and for 120  
days thereafter, no change, except by agreement of the parties, shall be made  
by the carrier or the employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute  
arose.
1-104. Expiration.  The Emergency Board shall terminate ninety (90) days after  
the submission of the report provided for in paragraph 1-102 of this Order.

It creates a board to investigate the dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain labor organizations. Inventory: the order is a board order whose operative commands are 1 clause(s) as recorded in the dossier (whole). The list of parties attached to the order identifies the dispute and is not a separate command. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12393, whose subject line describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute. Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadlines, option C): the report date and the end of any statutory standstill are spent facts that do not end the order; they are not recorded as later events because no report text is among this packet’s citable evidence, so the claim states the functional spending without a date. The packet’s number-citation lookup over the held order texts (33,118 readable files) found no held text citing this order by number other than its own printings.
